semantics.core1: compact semantic orientation; map, not teaching construction

hard_transitions.title: An equation constrains an unknown
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners arriving from arithmetic read the equals sign as an instruction to compute, and that reading survives unless it is confronted directly.

hard_transitions.title: Operations that preserve the solution set
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The steps are memorable as a procedure, which is exactly why the reversibility condition behind them goes unnoticed until it fails.

hard_transitions.title: An exact solution is not its decimal approximation
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Calculator habits teach that a decimal is the finished answer, so a fraction reads as unfinished work rather than as the exact value.

buckets.subject: Mathematics
buckets.title: Linear equations in one variable (Class VI to VIII bridge) and in two variables (Class IX)

hard_transitions.title: Solving an equation with the variable on both sides: the same operation on both sides, and transposing a variable term like a number
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The steps are routine, but two errors recur: changing one side only, and moving a term across the equality sign without changing its sign.

hard_transitions.title: Reducing an equation to simpler form: opening brackets, combining like terms and clearing denominators before solving
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Each reduction is familiar arithmetic, but a negative factor in front of a bracket, a term left unmultiplied by the LCM, and a vanishing variable each produce confident wrong answers.

hard_transitions.title: Linear equations in two variables: the form ax + by + c = 0, infinitely many solution pairs, and the straight-line graph
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners arrive expecting one number as the answer; here a solution is a pair, there are infinitely many, and the same statement can have one solution on a number line but infinitely many on the plane.

hard_transitions.title: Charge flow is not consumed by a component
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Everyday language about using electricity makes it easy to confuse energy transfer with disappearance of charge flow.

hard_transitions.title: Ohmic behavior is a tested model, not a permanent label
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The learner must separate a measured proportional pattern from the stronger claim that every device keeps one resistance under every operating condition.

buckets.subject: Physics
buckets.title: Fluid statics, buoyancy and Bernoulli flow

hard_transitions.title: Buoyant force follows displaced fluid
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The key distinction is between the object's own mass and the volume of fluid removed by the submerged part.

hard_transitions.title: Steady incompressible flow speeds up in a narrower section
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The rung requires a conserved through-flow picture rather than the everyday intuition that less room means slower motion.

hard_transitions.title: Pressure, speed and height trade along an ideal-flow path
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The main failure is using a two-variable slogan when the energy ledger also contains height and model conditions.

buckets.subject: Physics
buckets.title: Universal gravitation, free fall and orbital motion

hard_transitions.title: Gravity is a persistent mutual attraction fixed by source-receiver geometry
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners often make gravity one-sided, motion-dependent, or page-down; the rung must keep body ownership and geometric direction explicit.

hard_transitions.title: Universal gravitation: model scope, centre distance and inverse-square scaling
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The fragile move is not arithmetic: it is deciding whether the point/external-spherical model applies, defining centre-to-centre r, and keeping mass factors separate from the inverse-square distance factor.

hard_transitions.title: Local gravitational acceleration: force per unit mass and free-fall mass independence
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners can conflate force with field/acceleration, treat 9.8 m/s^2 as universal, or assume a heavier object must accelerate more because it feels a larger gravitational force.

hard_transitions.title: Mass stays with the object; weight is its local gravitational force
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Everyday language and scale readings encourage mass/weight conflation; the learner must keep object mass, local g, and gravitational force as different quantities.

hard_transitions.title: Gravitational binding uses a chosen zero of potential energy
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The rung must keep potential, kinetic, and total energy distinct while comparing bound motion with just-escape motion.

hard_transitions.title: Central gravity conserves orbital angular momentum about the centre
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The rung is both an origin condition and an axial-direction distinction, so the orbital plane and viewing side must remain explicit.

hard_transitions.title: Path travelled is not start-to-finish change
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Everyday language often uses distance for both ideas, so an out-and-back case is needed to force the distinction.

hard_transitions.title: Zero velocity at an instant does not mean zero acceleration
hard_transitions.badge_reason: A single still-looking instant invites learners to confuse the current velocity with how velocity is changing.

hard_transitions.title: Average speed and average velocity come from different totals
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The arithmetic is simple, but equal-distance and equal-time weighting are easily confused.

hard_transitions.title: Derive the constant-acceleration equations from one velocity-time graph
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The algebra is elementary, but the learner must connect graph slope and geometric area to three equivalent kinematic equations while preserving the model condition.

hard_transitions.title: Uniform circular motion keeps speed while velocity turns
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Everyday use of 'speed' and 'velocity' can hide that direction change alone is a velocity change.

hard_transitions.title: Motion graphs turn coordinate change into rate
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The arithmetic is simple, but graph height, slope, and physical motion are easily confused.

hard_transitions.title: Circular dynamics: centripetal is a net-force role, not a new force
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The same motion requirement can be supplied by different physical interactions, so learners must separate force type from radial role and re-declare the inward axis around the circle.

findings.detail: The declared primary representation has no scene instance bound to Core1.

hard_transitions.title: Split one plane-motion event into independent x/y components with one clock
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners often interpret independent components as unrelated motions and accidentally use different times or mix x and y quantities.

hard_transitions.title: Apply constant-acceleration kinematics component by component
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The formulas are familiar from 1D, but the challenge is selecting the right component equation on each axis and enforcing one common time.

hard_transitions.title: Select the gravity-only projectile model before using projectile consequences
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Projectile formulas become brittle when the learner skips the model decision, mixes times, or treats horizontal velocity as requiring a continuing horizontal force.

findings.detail: The declared primary representation has no scene instance bound to Core1.

hard_transitions.title: One magnetic direction, several page marks
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The learner must coordinate a three-dimensional axial direction with two-dimensional page marks before later magnetic rules are readable.

hard_transitions.title: Through-going field depends on surface orientation
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The hard move is treating the surface as oriented and comparing how much field passes through it without changing either its size or the field.

hard_transitions.title: A perpendicular magnetic force redirects without speeding up
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners often transfer the everyday rule 'force means speeding up' to a case where force is everywhere sideways to the instantaneous motion.

buckets.subject: Physics
buckets.title: Newton's first law and free-body diagrams

hard_transitions.title: Zero net force allows steady motion
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Everyday friction makes continued motion look as if it needs a continuing push.

hard_transitions.title: Nonzero forces can cancel
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners often read a zero total as evidence that nothing is present instead of as cancellation among directed contributions.

hard_transitions.title: A free-body diagram belongs to one chosen body
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Equal-and-opposite partner forces look like natural cancellations until the learner asks which body each arrow actually acts on.

hard_transitions.title: An accelerating observer needs a declared pseudo-force convention
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The same physical interactions can be described by observers with different accelerations, and the extra convention is easy to omit when the observer is inside the accelerating vehicle.

hard_transitions.title: Net force, not any one force, sets acceleration
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The difficult step is completing a one-body force inventory before using the simple equation.

hard_transitions.title: Friction opposes relative sliding at a contact
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Friction is often memorized as 'opposite motion', which fails for driven or rolling contacts.

hard_transitions.title: Third-law partner forces act on different bodies
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Equal-and-opposite wording invites learners to cancel a pair that belongs to two different bodies.

hard_transitions.title: Quantitative static and kinetic friction conditions
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The difficult decision is not substituting mu N; it is determining the required tangential force, the actual normal reaction, and whether the contact can remain static.

hard_transitions.title: Connected bodies and a justified common acceleration
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners must distinguish a kinematic constraint from a force interaction and must not cancel internal forces inside individual-body equations.

hard_transitions.title: Ideal-string tension belongs to each body-specific FBD
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Equal tension is a model consequence, not a property of every rope/pulley setup, and the two tension arrows act on different bodies.

hard_transitions.title: One fixed-pulley string gives one length constraint
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The learner must translate geometry into one fixed-length equation rather than memorize a pulley-count rule.

hard_transitions.title: Force from a steady stream of discrete momentum changes
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The key decisions are the system/direction choice and distinguishing force on the ejecta from equal-and-opposite launcher recoil and the external support force that balances it.

hard_transitions.title: Measure reflection from the normal, not the surface
hard_transitions.badge_reason: A familiar mirror picture becomes wrong immediately if the reference line for the angle is the surface instead of the normal.

hard_transitions.title: Real and virtual describe how light paths meet
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The everyday word virtual invites a false not-recordable interpretation unless image type is tied directly to ray geometry.

hard_transitions.title: Optical signs come from declared directions
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Memorized object-and-image sign tables fail as soon as the drawing is mirrored or a less familiar optical configuration is used.

hard_transitions.title: Principal rays are consistent shortcuts to one spherical-mirror image
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners can memorize individual ray rules yet combine them inconsistently or treat one ray as sufficient to locate an image.

hard_transitions.title: The mirror equation is a signed paraxial model of the ray geometry
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Correct algebra can still represent the wrong physical mirror if signs are assigned from labels or if the paraxial model condition is forgotten.

hard_transitions.title: Signed magnification carries image size and orientation
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners often keep only the absolute size ratio and lose the orientation information carried by the sign.

hard_transitions.title: Refraction begins with the normal and the two media
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The visible ray kink is easy to copy while using the wrong angular reference or forgetting that a slab contains two separate boundaries.

hard_transitions.title: Refractive index connects speed change to Snell geometry
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners often remember a sine ratio but reverse the media or interpret higher refractive index as faster light.

hard_transitions.title: A thin lens image must be supported by independent principal rays
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Memorized image tables can hide incompatible ray rules or the false idea that a ray through the optical centre must bend strongly.

hard_transitions.title: Use the signed thin-lens equation only after the ray model fixes the geometry
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The algebra is short, but mirror/lens sign confusion and loss of the paraxial model boundary produce plausible-looking wrong answers.

hard_transitions.title: Lens magnification sign carries image orientation
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Using only |m| preserves size while erasing the erect/inverted information that the signed optical state contains.

hard_transitions.title: Lens power is signed inverse focal length in metres
hard_transitions.badge_reason: A correct reciprocal can still be wrong by a factor of one hundred if centimetres are substituted directly, and dropping sign erases converging/diverging character.

hard_transitions.title: Repetition is not enough: look for a stable equilibrium
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Repeated motion is visually salient, so learners can miss the stronger requirement that the system's response be organized around one stable equilibrium.

hard_transitions.title: Energy trades twice during one displacement cycle
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The position cycle repeats once while the energy pattern repeats at both center crossings, so learners must coordinate two time patterns without confusing sign with stored energy.

buckets.subject: Physics
buckets.title: Rotational dynamics, angular momentum and rolling

hard_transitions.title: Mass distribution sets rotational inertia about an axis
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The comparison is qualitative but only works if the axis stays explicit while the mass distribution changes.

hard_transitions.title: Angular momentum conservation belongs to a specified origin
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The central difficulty is keeping the turning-effect test and angular-momentum statement tied to the same origin while the body's distribution changes.

hard_transitions.title: Pure rolling makes the contact point instantaneously at rest
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The learner must combine translation with rotation at different points of one rigid body without treating every point as having the centre speed.

hard_transitions.title: Mass distribution changes ideal rolling acceleration
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The comparison is conceptual only if mass amount, radius, incline, and no-slip conditions are controlled while shape changes.

hard_transitions.title: A machine trades force or direction for distance; it does not create work
hard_transitions.badge_reason: A larger output force looks like an energy gain unless input distance is tracked.

hard_transitions.title: Levers, pulleys and inclined planes realize different force-distance tradeoffs
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners can memorize device names without identifying what each machine changes about force, direction and distance.

hard_transitions.title: Sound propagates through a medium as longitudinal compressions and rarefactions
hard_transitions.badge_reason: A transverse-looking sketch is tempting; the learner must keep local particle displacement parallel to propagation and read compression/rarefaction as density/pressure-pattern changes rather than travelling particles.

hard_transitions.title: Sound graphs separate amplitude, wavelength, period, frequency and speed
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Frequency, wavelength and amplitude can all change independently enough that verbal mixing is common.

hard_transitions.title: Reflected sound can form echoes, reverberation and echolocation cues
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The common arithmetic error is forgetting the round trip; a second modeling error is treating one memorized delay/distance threshold as universally defining an echo.

findings.detail: The declared primary representation has no scene instance bound to Core1.

hard_transitions.title: Internal energy is stored; heat and work are transfers
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The entry distinction must be made with a system boundary before any energy-balance law is introduced.

hard_transitions.title: Internal-energy change is fixed by endpoint states, not process path
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The learner must read a Cartesian pressure-volume diagram as multiple paths between the same endpoints without turning path area into a state property.

hard_transitions.title: A complete cycle returns the state while its loop records net work
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The rung depends on reading a directed closed pressure-volume loop while keeping state return separate from nonzero energy transfer over the cycle.

hard_transitions.title: Heat engines require heat rejection and obey a reservoir-temperature ceiling
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The distinction is conceptual: removing mechanical losses does not remove the second-law need for a cold-reservoir heat flow.

hard_transitions.title: Impose a component constraint on a resultant
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The learner must reverse the usual direction of reasoning: instead of finding the resultant from inputs, one resultant component is specified and an input component must be chosen to make it true.

hard_transitions.title: Add vectors by corresponding signed components
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The arithmetic is simple once the representation is correct, but learners often add magnitudes or mix unlike axes instead of combining corresponding signed components.

hard_transitions.title: Operand order reverses a subtraction result
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The construction may already be familiar, but learners can still preserve the same arrow direction after swapping the words.

hard_transitions.title: Resolve magnitude-and-angle vectors into signed perpendicular components
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The trigonometry is short, but learners must first decide whether decomposition is needed, identify the angle reference, preserve signs, and avoid treating an initial component pair as a later-time motion law.

hard_transitions.title: Translate signed components to i-hat/j-hat notation
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The notation is compact but can tempt learners to drop a negative coefficient or treat basis labels as extra vector magnitudes.

hard_transitions.title: Recover direction from signed components
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The ratio is simple, but a calculator's inverse tangent does not by itself preserve quadrant information.

hard_transitions.title: Normalize a nonzero vector to unit direction
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The division is simple, but the same magnitude must divide every component and the zero vector is a hard domain boundary.

hard_transitions.title: Only the along-path part of a force contributes to work
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Force size alone feels decisive until a strong perpendicular force is contrasted with the actual displacement.

hard_transitions.title: Net work sign tracks kinetic-energy change
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners may attach energy change to one named force rather than to the combined work of all forces.

hard_transitions.title: Potential energy belongs only to endpoint-determined interactions
hard_transitions.badge_reason: It is tempting to hide every force inside an energy label, especially once gravitational potential energy is familiar.

hard_transitions.title: Mechanical energy is constant only after the system and transfer account close
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The familiar K+U equality is easy to apply before declaring the system or checking friction/external transfer, which confuses total-energy conservation with the narrower mechanical-energy shortcut.

hard_transitions.title: Power is an energy-transfer rate, not the work itself
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Learners often keep the same units and reasoning for work and power or treat an interval average as an instantaneous value.

hard_transitions.title: Grade 9 work and mechanical-energy equations are one ledger
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The arithmetic is direct; the difficult part is deciding which account and relation the situation permits.

hard_transitions.title: Derive kinetic and raised-body potential energy from the work ledger
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The endpoint formulae are simple; the harder work is maintaining one physical model through the force, motion and work substitutions.

hard_transitions.title: A number alone does not say where something is
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The idea is reachable by pacing a room, but it is routinely skipped as obvious and then assumed by every rung above it.

hard_transitions.title: Position measured from the other object
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Observer order and common time are easily hidden by a memorized formula.

hard_transitions.title: From relative position to relative velocity
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The student must connect two same-time position statements to one common interval rather than memorize a subtraction rule.

hard_transitions.title: Check direction, magnitude and observer reversal
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Correct arithmetic can conceal an incorrect vector construction or frame interpretation.

hard_transitions.title: Vector information versus magnitude-only information
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The words are simple, but learners often treat equal length or equal speed as if it fully identifies a directed quantity.

hard_transitions.title: Choosing axes and keeping components signed
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Axis choice is conventional, but once the positive directions are declared the component signs are fixed and cannot be chosen for convenience.

hard_transitions.title: Subtraction as addition of the reversed vector
hard_transitions.badge_reason: The reverse-then-add construction is a genuine model shift from ordinary addition, even though the component arithmetic looks similar.

hard_transitions.title: When the simple v_A/B = v_A - v_B relation needs frame qualification (research-boundary note)
hard_transitions.badge_reason: Not a Grade 9 assessment badge: this is a RESEARCH-depth boundary note, included only to show where the taught relation stops applying.
